correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and 0<=k<n, allowed 2-path shortening yields e(i,j)=P(i,j) modulo explicit integral two-boundaries, so H_1 is generated by the Hamiltonian unit cycle. If 2k<n, the integer positive-residue functional on every regular ordered pair kills the boundary of each allowed 2-path, even when the shortcut is forbidden, and evaluates to n on the unit cycle. Thus H_1=Z with no torsion. At k*=ceil(n/2), the regular backtrack (0,k*,0), together with two explicit telescoping shortening sums, is an allowed integral 2-chain of exactly n-1 terms with boundary the Hamiltonian cycle, so H_1=0 thereafter. Inclusions preserve the literal generator and H_0 connects at k=1. The executable independent finite boundary-span model checks 65 cases over four primes and 28 literal integer fillings, but infinite validity rests on the displayed integral proof.

value.rationale: The natural edge-thickening filtration of a directed circle has a genuine topological transition: its only degree-one path-homology class survives every nonreciprocal forward-power stage and dies exactly at the first reciprocal edge. Determining the sharp death endpoint closes a specific gap left by the published interval-circulant theorem and gives the entire integral low-degree barcode, not just a sampled Betti number or an Euler characteristic. A uniform n-1-cell integral filling explicitly explains the mechanism. Its independent mathematical utility is an exact reproducible benchmark for persistent directed topology with a sharp graph-theoretic trigger; no higher-dimensional claims or large downstream consequences are asserted.
